summary: JSON.parse converts valid JSON text into JavaScript values.
documentation: JSON.parse converts valid JSON text into JavaScript values. JSON supports objects, arrays, strings, numbers, Booleans and null. Invalid JSON raises SyntaxError instead of returning a partial result.
inputs: JSON text and an optional reviver callback.
returns: The JavaScript value represented by the text.
caution: Parsing does not validate application structure or make later object merges safe. Never use eval to parse JSON.
scenarios: Read a saved local configuration snapshot.
Decode a downloaded JSON report before validating its fields.
Restore structured settings stored as text.
title: Decode a saved JSON value
problem: Input is a valid JSON string representing any JSON value. Return the parsed value. Numbers are finite and within the safe-integer range when integral. Do not return the input text unchanged.
goal: Use JSON.parse() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Parse the text directly with JSON.parse.
